_doc: Every correction made to Public Ledger, newest first on the page (tools/build_corrections.py). One entry per correction: date (ISO, the day it went live), where (the page or pages), was (what was wrong, with a figure where there was one), now (what the site says instead and how it is checked from now on). Optional: reported (ISO, the day the problem was reported); once entries carry it the page states the median days from report to fix. Add an entry with every correction; never remove one.

entries.where: The decisions register: each resolution's title (its record, its row, the search, its share page), and the votes of a few records
entries.was: 884 resolutions showed a title their own minutes do not print. B-008-23, the 11-3 adoption of the 2024 budget, read "Budget Modification Sales Tax" and IL-136-22, the Hartland Town Park grant, read "Ewings Road Resurfacing Change Order No. I - Final": where an agenda prints its numbers as one column and its entries as another, the last number took the first entry. Others read a category header ("APPOINTMENTS:", PW-001-15), a budget table's sub-heading ("INCREASE ANTICIPATED REVENUE:", IF-022-22), a sponsor list (36), a title cut short, "title not machine-readable" (38) where the minutes print a legible one, or words the heading does not print (IL-026-22 read "Carousel Park Association Inc.", an agenda's "- DSS" or "- Treasurer": 540). The same reading gave a few votes to the wrong record: 38 heads printed "From;" were not read as heads, two minutes files store their pages out of order or reprint one (5-17-22, 8-6-24), a citation was read as a head (CW-004-15), and seven heads whose number the text layer misread became rows of their own ("CS-925-22" for CS-025-22). IL-021-21, referred to committee, showed as adopted 14-0; IF-135-24 showed a vote its minutes do not print.
entries.now: Every title is set beside the heading its own block in the minutes prints. Where they name different things, or the register's title adds words the heading does not print, the record shows the minutes' title and says "Title as printed in the minutes" (1,183 records, floor items included); the earlier title is kept in the data. Agenda columns are paired with their entries only when the counts match, "From;" heads are read, the two files are read in the order their text runs, and a misread number goes to the listed resolution its title names. 5,829 votes are read (was 5,787), each on its own record; the seven phantom rows are gone and CS-017-20, missing before, is listed: 6,099 resolutions. The build stops if an outlined record shows a title its block does not print.

entries.where: Legislators (every member's no votes) and the decisions register (who voted no)
entries.was: A member's no votes counted only the noes the minutes name, and the reader lost names where a long list wrapped onto a second line or a scan read a letter as a digit ("Vi1tuoso"). Irene M. Myers and Rebecca J. Wydysh read 0 no votes, though the Dec 9, 2025 minutes name both voting no on B-04-25; 60 of the 104 votes with a no named fewer noes than their count, and the December budget-amendment votes, whose minutes name only the ayes, counted against no one.
entries.now: Every printed list is read in full (49 votes). Where the minutes name only the ayes and the absent, the noes are the rest of that year's seated chamber, worked out only when ayes, noes and absent add up to the 15 seats, and marked "worked out" on the vote and the record (30 votes). The 25 votes whose minutes print the count alone are left out of every member's count and rate, and each record says so. Myers now reads 15 no votes, Wydysh 15. The build stops if a list of noes reads short of its count.

entries.where: The decisions register (a resolution's money line)
entries.was: A figure the resolution's own text says was budgeted, or is the amount appropriated, was labeled "Revenue accepted" (15 resolutions). Among them, B-04-25, rejected 3-11, read "Revenue accepted $100,700,000": that is the sales tax the 2026 budget already held; the resolution asked to add $3,045,592.
entries.now: Those figures read as amounts mentioned in the text. A resolution that failed says what it proposed ("Revenue it proposed", "Largest budget change it proposed: $3,045,592"), never "accepted" or "awarded", and the build checks every failed resolution's labels.

entries.was: The topic rules filed 47 of a random 200 resolutions where a reader would not look for them: grants of community partnership funding as statements of position, consultants' amendments and sole-source purchases as everything else, a consulting firm hired for brownfield grant services as People & positions.
entries.now: The rules were fixed and 1,089 resolutions changed topic. The hand check is published with both readings for each of the 200 (data/topic-check-2026-10-31.json), and the build stops if the rules change without a new check.

entries.was: The county and city rates came from the state's open-data table, which rounds them to two decimals: a $250,000 home read $1,385 of county tax and $6,077 in all.
entries.now: The latest year's county and city rates are the State Comptroller's full-precision rates, each checked against the open-data table's two decimals; the same home reads $1,386 of county tax and $6,078 in all.

entries.where: Past meetings (the key under each meeting's bar)
entries.was: The Oct 30 correction fixed the first screen's bars only: the key under each meeting in Past meetings still read "Water/sewer/golf" (and "Water, sewer & golf" to a screen reader) on nights with no golf-course lines, including Oct 20, 2026, whose $117,334 is water and sewer.
entries.now: The key, its spoken label and the first screen name each night's slice by the funds it holds ("Water & sewer"), from one function.

entries.was: Lockport, Dunkirk, Olean and Batavia were shown at their surrounding town's tax rate, not the city's: Lockport's city line read 4.24 per $1,000 for FY2025 when the city's published rate is 10.42.
entries.now: Each city is matched by its own state code (SWIS), and the build stops if a city's rate does not match the state's published rate for that year.

entries.where: Warrant dates (council briefs, the register, the feed)
entries.was: Seven warrants were dated by the day their report was printed rather than the council meeting that approved them; the brief for the Aug 19, 2025 meeting said Aug 15, 2025.
entries.now: Every warrant is dated by the meeting in the city's own file name, with the printed date shown beside it where it differs.

entries.was: On a night with two warrants the headline gave the larger one only: "$1.59 million" for Oct 20, 2026, when the council approved $1,641,618 that night.
entries.now: The headline, the Past meetings card, each council brief and the feed state one total for the whole meeting.

entries.where: The front page's "Where it went" bars
entries.was: A bar was labelled "Water, sewer & golf" on a night with no golf-course lines in it.
entries.now: The bar names only the funds it holds that night ("Water & sewer").

entries.was: A city employee's petty-cash account was listed by name among vendors that might belong on a contract.
entries.now: Petty-cash accounts are not vendors and are left out of that flag; the names of private individuals the city pays are withheld across the site (each line keeps its amount, account and page).
